title: Commentariorum In Epistolam Beati Pauli Ad Titum Liber Unus
author: Jerome

passages.original: Montanus et qui Novati schisma sectantur, nomen sibi munditiae prae- sumpsere : putantque secunda matrimonia ab Eccle- siae communione prohibenda : cum Apostolus de episcopis et presbyteris hoc praecipiens, utique in caeteris relaxarit : non quod hortetur ad secunda matrimonia(??); sed quod necessitati carnis indulgeat. Scripsit et Tertullianus de Monogamia librum hae- reticum : quem Apostolo contraire, nemo qui Apo- stolum legerit, ignorabit. Et quidem esse sine cri- mine episcopum, sive presbyterum, et unam uxorem habere, in nostra est potestate.
passages.english: Montanus, and those who follow the schism of Novatus, have presumptuously claimed for themselves the name of purity, and they think that second marriages should be barred from the communion of the Church, although the Apostle, in laying this down for bishops and presbyters, has certainly relaxed [it] for the rest; not that he urges [people] to second marriages, but that he makes allowance for the necessity of the flesh. Tertullian too wrote a heretical book, On Monogamy, which no one who has read the Apostle will fail to see runs contrary to the Apostle. And indeed, for a bishop or presbyter to be without reproach and to have one wife is within our power.
passages.notes: "Novati": Jerome names Novatus, though the rigorist schism meant is usually associated with Novatian; the two names are often confused in antiquity. The edition's "(??)" after "matrimonia" is a printed query mark and has been left untranslated.
